nobox.final_span:
. Now a pro-life speaker, Johnson discussed her journey on the panel at the Belo Center for New Media.
Johnson described herself as feeling very depressed following the life-changing experience, using alcohol, food, and exercise to cope with it. She said that the experience prompted in her a feeling of disconnection from God’s forgiveness. She said she ultimately prayed to God for help, and stated she feels God led her out of that time period, forgiving her and supporting her in ways she cannot articulate.
Konzelman responded to the criticism by saying that people do not remember that in order to portray a part of Johnson’s story, they changed her name, and it would not be illegal, if they showed it on film. He stated that he considered film to be a distinct form of communication compared to a written documentary.
Johnson, speaking to the Argus, explained how crucial it was to remind Americans about current practices for carrying out abortions.
Johnson also talked about her religious conversion during a recent appearance on “Shalom in the Home,” a daily TV program aired from the Holy Lands, available nightly on Line 4 at EWTN.
Johnson, whose visit to the Holy Lands was extensive, wrote about its physical and emotional effects on her in a recent appearance on the radio program, “Writing Well with Dr. Wendy”, aired February 4 on Fountain Square MediaRadio.
Johnson described the impact of the Christian sites in the Holy Land on her, and how that impact became even stronger now that she is Catholic.
Johnson also shared her experiences, both from history and personally, on "Conversation with Cardinal," titled "Wissam's Kingdom," a show hosted by Cardinal Wissam Aydзна in Egypt.
Johnson, featured in a new book by Pope Francis, has also visited Project Pearls, Hillcrest Women’s Center, and Door Village Chapel, as stated on her website. She wrote her autobiography, “UnPlanned: Stories of the Dr. Dreamers and Defenders and the Savior,” and she is the founder of And Then There Were None (ATTWN), an organization designed to bring companies out of the abortion business, according to her website.
